purpose: Per-style corpus for Tier-0 in-text citation detection (refcheck.extraction.intext_signals). Every case pins what a marker family looks like in one citation style, or pins a construct that must NOT be read as a citation. The corpus exists because the two failure directions here are not symmetric: a missed marker costs a check that isn't run, while a spurious one is displayed to a reviewer as an 'orphaned citation' — a report of an authoring error that isn't there. Most of the exclusion cases therefore carry more weight than the detection cases.
layout: One file per citation style (apa7.json, german_apa.json, chicago_authordate.json, ieee.json, vancouver.json), plus exclusions.json for constructs that collide with a marker regardless of style. Style files are named to line up with fixtures/citation_styles/, so a style whose bibliography parsing and whose in-text markers both need work is one name in two places rather than two vocabularies.
relationship_to_citation_styles: This is a sibling of fixtures/citation_styles, not an extension of it. That corpus is a regression record: each case reproduces a specific parser failure at a specific commit, and its 'reproduces' block is what proves the case can distinguish a fixed parser from a broken one. This corpus has no such history — the detector is new — so cases here state the behaviour they pin and nothing more. Inventing 'reproduces' blocks for cases that never failed anywhere would look like the same evidence while carrying none.
provenance: Independently authored synthetic text. Author surnames, years, page numbers and sentence content are invented; nothing is copied from a real manuscript, a library PDF, or any third-party citation checker's source, tests or fixtures (see docs/clean-room-development-policy.md and AGENTS.md). The marker grammars themselves come from the public style rules the styles are named after.

case_schema.id: Unique across all files; appears in the pytest test id.
case_schema.note: What this case pins, and why it is a case at all.
case_schema.text: The body text to run detection over, exactly as the detector sees it.
case_schema.families: Optional. The marker families to restrict detection to, as detect_citations' families argument would receive them from expected_families(). Omitted means 'search for everything', which is what a document with no clear bibliography evidence gets.

expect.citations: The full expected result, in order. One entry per reference, so a grouped marker has several entries sharing a marker string. Fields left out default to null (authors, year, number) or false (narrative). An empty list is the assertion that nothing is detected.

maintenance: A case that must change is a behaviour decision, not a test fix — say so in the commit message. When adding a detection pattern, add its exclusion counterpart in the same change: every pattern that widens detection has a construct it can now collide with, and the collision is the part that reaches a reviewer.

what_this_corpus_cannot_see.boundary: This corpus stops at detection: it pins what intext_signals reads out of body text, and nothing beyond it. Which reference a marker resolves to, where its span sits in the document, and what its context passage contains are decided downstream in extraction/citation_matching.py and extraction/document_artifact.py, over which no case here has any reach. A change to the matcher can leave every case in this corpus green while being wrong about all of them.
what_this_corpus_cannot_see.the_scoring_constants: The matcher's numeric constants are the sharpest form of that blind spot. Every one was perturbed in BOTH directions on 2026-08-14 and the full suite re-run after each, which is the only way to find out what actually depends on a value. SURNAME_MATCH_THRESHOLD 0.90 → 0.50 fails 13 tests, 0.90 → 0.99 fails 10, both including behavioural ones. _MISSING_YEAR_PENALTY 0.9 → 0.1 fails 3, and 0.9 → 0.99 fails the 3 that were added the same day to cover its upper edge. _POSITIONAL_NUMBER_CONFIDENCE 0.5 → 0.99 fails test_a_positional_number_does_not_claim_certainty; 0.5 → 0.01 fails nothing, and should not, because its only documented property is that it stays below SURNAME_MATCH_THRESHOLD and lowering it keeps that true. None of the three is pinned by name outside test_citation_matching.py.
what_this_corpus_cannot_see.the_correction_that_produced_this_entry: An earlier version of this note said _MISSING_YEAR_PENALTY was 'covered anyway' and that SURNAME_MATCH_THRESHOLD was 'the one nothing behavioural depends on'. Both were wrong, and wrongly for the same reason: each rested on a single perturbation. The penalty documents two properties — large enough that an exact name survives a missing date, small enough that a merely similar one does not — and 0.9 sits on the floor of that band, so moving it down broke the first property loudly while the whole upper half of the range was silent until 2026-08-14. A review (Fable 5) found the gap by moving it up: at 0.99, '(Fisher, 2020)' resolves against a dateless 'Fischer' entry, which is exactly the false match the 0.90 threshold was raised to prevent, reached through the other constant. The threshold claim was a second-hand memory of the 0.80 → 0.90 raise, made before the pair assertions existed; today that constant is well covered and the note simply had not been re-measured.
what_this_corpus_cannot_see.corpus_blindness_is_not_suite_blindness: Keep the two apart, because conflating them is what made the claim above sound safe. The 121-citation recall corpus resolves identically at every threshold from 0.0 to 1.0 — year agreement carries all of the discrimination in those five documents and names carry none (test_citation_matching_recall.py, and test_the_threshold_does_not_decide_anything_on_this_corpus, which asserts that sweep rather than leaving it as a claim). That is a fact about the corpus and stays true. What covers these constants is constructed cases written for the argument each value rests on, not documents; 'the corpus cannot see it' is a reason to write those cases, never a licence to skip them.
what_this_corpus_cannot_see.rule: Before arguing a scoring constant from a green suite, find out whether the suite can see it: perturb it and run the suite. Perturb it in BOTH directions, and once per documented property — a constant justified by two clauses has two edges, and a test on one of them looks exactly like a test on the constant. If something fails, the failures say what depends on the value. If nothing fails but a bare-value pin, the suite is reporting nothing: justify the value from the pairs it was chosen against, measured and asserted individually, and write them down beside the constant, as SURNAME_MATCH_THRESHOLD's comment and _MISSING_YEAR_PENALTY's band do. Keep the bare pin as a change detector, but noticing a value moved is not evidence the new value is right.
